text:
Seattle is 11-10-1 and has been outplayed more often than the record shows. The Kraken get 45.9% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and have scored about five more goals than those chances predict. Our numbers give them a 27% shot at the playoffs, and the last ten (4-6-0) have been rough.

The best thing happening is Berkly Catton. He set a franchise milestone with his first NHL hat trick, has nine points in his last ten, and Daily Faceoff asked whether he is the game-breaking talent Seattle has been missing. The other big move went the other way: on Nov. 1 the Kraken traded Shane Wright, the fourth overall pick in 2022, to Nashville for Matthew Wood. Wright had been centering Catton and Kaapo Kakko. Alison Lukan's notes say Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich have been driving play since.

The worry is the penalty kill. After a 4-3 loss in San Jose, Lane Lambert called it "the elephant in the room," per Lukan, after two power-play goals against. Jordan Eberle scored his 100th goal with the franchise in a 3-1 loss in Chicago, and Freddy Gaudreau reached 500 NHL games. The Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann line has been the weak spot, 39% of the chances, and McMann has two points in ten. Fixing the kill and that line is the season's to-do list.
headline: Berkly Catton is the Kraken's reason to watch
